meta.description: Checks OpenShift CronJobs in a project/namespace and emails you when the latest run failed or appears to have been missed.

parameters.content:
## OpenShift CronJob Monitor

**What it does**
1. Runs on a schedule
2. Reads CronJobs + recent Jobs from your OpenShift project
3. Emails you if a watched CronJob failed or looks missed

**Edit these first**
1. **Config** node — API URL, namespace, cronjob names, email, thresholds
2. Create an n8n **Header Auth** credential named `OpenShift SA Token`
   - Name: `Authorization`
   - Value: `Bearer <service-account-token>`
3. Create an n8n **SMTP** credential (or swap the Email node for Gmail/Outlook)
4. Activate the workflow

**OpenShift SA needs** `get/list` on `cronjobs` and `jobs` in the target namespace.

nodes.name: Every 15 Minutes
nodes.notes: Change the interval to match how often you want to poll OpenShift.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: EDIT ME: set cluster API URL, project/namespace, comma-separated CronJob names, grace period, and alert email addresses.

parameters.content:
## Config tips

- `cronJobNames`: comma-separated list, e.g. `exam-calendar-sync,nightly-backup`
- Leave blank to watch **all** CronJobs in the namespace
- `missedGraceMinutes`: how long after the schedule before a missing successful run is an alert
- `jobLookbackHours`: only inspect Jobs newer than this window

nodes.name: Get CronJobs
nodes.notes: Attach Header Auth credential: Authorization = Bearer <token>. Toggle allowUnauthorizedCerts off if your cluster has a trusted CA.

nodes.name: Get Jobs
nodes.notes: Uses the same OpenShift SA token credential as Get CronJobs.

nodes.name: Analyze CronJob Health
nodes.notes: Detects failed Jobs, missed successful runs after lastScheduleTime, missing CronJobs, and suspended CronJobs.

nodes.name: Send Alert Email
nodes.notes: Attach your SMTP credential here. You can replace this node with Gmail, Microsoft Outlook, or another mail node if preferred.

parameters.content:
## Auth setup (OpenShift)

```bash
oc create sa n8n-cron-monitor -n your-project-name
oc policy add-role-to-user view system:serviceaccount:your-project-name:n8n-cron-monitor -n your-project-name
oc create token n8n-cron-monitor -n your-project-name --duration=8760h
```

Put the token in n8n Header Auth as:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`

API URL example:
`https://api.cluster.example.com:6443`
